memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Jacob heard that his daughter Dinah had been defiled, his sons were in the fields with his livestock; so he did nothing about it until they came home. Then Shechem's father Hamor went out to talk with Jacob. Meanwhile, Jacob's sons had come in from the fields as soon as they heard what had happened. They were shocked and furious, because Shechem had done an outrageous thing in Israel by sleeping with Jacob's daughter—a thing that should not be done." - Gen 34:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two reactions meet here. Jacob, the father, hears that his daughter has been violated — and "he did nothing." His strange silence is troubling; a wrong this deep called for a father's protective response, yet Jacob waits passively. His sons, by contrast, come in from the fields "shocked and furious." Their anger was right and fitting: an outrageous thing had been done, "a thing that should not be done."

There is an important truth here about anger. Not all anger is sinful. When we are stirred to fury by genuine evil — the abuse of the innocent, cruelty, injustice — that anger reflects something of God's own heart, for God hates injustice too. The brothers were right to be outraged.

But as this chapter will sadly show, righteous anger can go terribly wrong in how it is expressed. The question is never only "Is my anger justified?" but also "What will I do with it?" Anger at evil is holy; but if we let it drive us to sin, we ruin a right feeling with a wrong response.

Scripture says, "In your anger do not sin" (Eph 4:26). When injustice rightly stirs you, bring that fire to God. Let it move you toward what is good and just, not toward revenge. Feel the wrong deeply — but do not let a righteous anger lead you into unrighteous action.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I let genuine evil stir a holy anger in me?
2. When I am angry, what do I do with it — good or harm?
3. Where do I need to bring my anger to God before I act?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a heart that burns against real injustice, as Yours does. But keep my anger from turning into sin. Help me to bring my anger to You and to respond in ways that honour You. Amen.
